title: India Moves to Bring Home Dammam Victim's Remains as Injured Indians Leave Hospital
excerpt: In an October 23 advisory, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh said it is assisting the family of the Indian killed at King Fahd International Airport, one injured Indian was discharged on October 22 and the second was expected out on October 23.
body:
• India's Embassy in Riyadh said on October 23 it is in touch with the family of the Indian killed in the October 21 Dammam airport attack and is extending all assistance to transport his mortal remains to India.
  • Of the two Indians injured at Dammam, one was discharged on October 22 and the other was expected to be discharged on October 23, the embassy's 17:00 hrs advisory said.
  • The Indian injured in the separate Shaybah oil field attack was also discharged on October 22.
  • Indians in Saudi Arabia: follow the embassy advisory — take precautions, move indoors during aerial attacks, and do not photograph or share images of interceptions or impact sites, which can breach Saudi law.

India is facilitating the return home of the mortal remains of the Indian national killed in the October 21 attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, and the two Indians injured in that attack are leaving hospital, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh said in an updated advisory on October 23.

The development moves the story beyond the casualty confirmation reported a day earlier. In our earlier coverage, Indian Killed in Dammam Airport Attack, Embassy Confirms New Toll, repatriation arrangements had not yet been released and the injured were still receiving care.

What the October 23 advisory says

"One Indian national tragically lost his life in the attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on 21 October. The Embassy is in touch with his family and is extending all necessary assistance to facilitate the transportation of his mortal remains to India," the embassy said in its update issued at 17:00 hrs on October 23, reported by ANI.

"The Embassy is in touch with his family and is extending all necessary assistance to facilitate the transportation of his mortal remains to India."

— Indian Embassy in Riyadh, advisory, October 23, 2026

On the injured, the advisory gave a hospital picture that had not been available before. Among the two Indian nationals injured in the Dammam airport attack, one person was discharged on October 22 and the other was expected to be discharged on October 23. The Indian national injured in the attack on the Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province was discharged on October 22.

The wider casualty picture

The Dammam attack on the evening of October 21 killed two people — one Indian resident and one Saudi citizen — according to Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA). Eight people were injured, including two Indians, two Yemenis, two Bangladeshis, one Saudi citizen and one Nepali resident, with injuries ranging from minor to critical. Airport operations have since resumed and air traffic has returned to normal, GACA said.

The embassy advisory also updated the earlier Riyadh airport attack of October 10. Two Indians injured in that attack are still receiving treatment in intensive care and two others remain in a normal ward, while seven injured Indian nationals have been discharged to date. One Indian was killed in the Riyadh attack and his funeral was held in Riyadh on October 12, the embassy said.

India's Ministry of External Affairs has strongly condemned the attacks on Dammam airport and the Shaybah oil field, calling strikes on civilian and critical infrastructure "completely unacceptable" and expressing solidarity with Saudi Arabia, according to earlier MEA statements reported by Nation Press and IANS.

Help and precautions for Indians in Saudi Arabia

Saudi Arabia is home to about 2.74 million Indian nationals, one of India's largest overseas communities. The embassy thanked Saudi authorities for the medical care provided to the injured and repeated its safety guidance for the community.

"The Indian community is urged to take due precautions and abide by Saudi laws especially those relating to not taking or sharing photos or videos of interceptions, impact sites etc.," the advisory said. Earlier embassy guidance advised nationals to proceed to the nearest safe place inside a building or an interior room away from windows during an aerial attack.

The embassy and the Consulate General in Jeddah have also been running 24x7 control rooms and working with airlines and tour operators on the return of Umrah pilgrims, with about 3,000 stranded pilgrims and more than 10,000 regular pilgrims returned to India over the past week, according to the MEA.

What happens next

The embassy has not announced a date for the arrival of the Dammam victim's remains in India or released his identity in the advisory. Families awaiting discharge and repatriation updates should follow the embassy's official advisories, which remain the authoritative source as the situation in the region continues to change.
